attribution.note: Marcus's own closing sentence in his post. It is not a quotation from the complaint.

semantics.note: The proposition restates the sentence accurately, naming Sam and Greg as Altman and Brockman. It is a retrospective comparison with no hedge.

contract.note: The plain reading (substantial departure from the founding commitments on nonprofit purpose, openness and investor returns) is fair and ordinary. Excluding later restructuring is right. Because no threshold is given, the result depends on how the commitments are weighed.

evidence.note: Founding baseline: nonprofit, value for everyone, researchers encouraged to publish. It also expected work with companies.
The 2019 capped-profit LP brought in investor returns, a real departure. The same post keeps nonprofit control, which limits how far it supports the claim.
A 2023 interview in which the chief scientist admits a reversal on research sharing, citing competition.
November 2023 company disclosure: the nonprofit board governs, a majority of directors are independent and hold no equity. This shows continuity in governance.
After the November 2023 crisis, Microsoft got a non-voting observer seat, not control. This weighs against the claim that the original model was entirely replaced.

reviews.rationale: The records show real departures on research openness and on freedom from investor returns (e2, e3). But formal nonprofit governance and mission obligations continued up to the post (e2, e4, e5). Under the contract, that continuity weighs against the breadth of 'little to do with'. The departure part holds; the sweeping 'little to do with' part is not borne out.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assessment of the complaint. He is not quoting it.

semantics.note: 'I take... to be largely accurate' states a firm judgment, not a probability. Leaving out the remark about unnamed news reports is acceptable.

contract.note: The plain reading (the complaint's central factual narrative is substantially correct) is fair. Separating facts from legal theories and from the AGI characterisations is reasonable.

evidence.note: Confirms the founding as a nonprofit, one background fact in the complaint. It does not confirm the alleged agreement or its breach.
OpenAI's interested account of the 2017 for-profit negotiations, published before the cutoff. It complicates the complaint's narrative but does not refute it.
The 2026 trial was decided on the statute of limitations, not on whether the complaint's facts were accurate.

reviews.rationale: Only the founding background is independently confirmed (e1). The core claims (a binding founding agreement, a departure from it, GPT-4 as AGI, a de facto Microsoft subsidiary) are contested by an interested party (e2), and no merits finding exists, since the case was decided on limitations (e3). The packet does not settle whether the complaint is largely accurate.

attribution.note: Marcus's own characterisation of what the lawsuit adds.

semantics.note: The testable core is kept: the lawsuit adds evidence on Altman's candor. 'Makes a good read' is opinion and is rightly dropped.

contract.note: Requiring specific, corroborated statements that support an inference of misleading communication is a fair reading of 'further evidence'. The contract rightly flags the shift from candor with the board to candor with Musk.

evidence.note: The complaint quotes a specific Altman assurance. It is an allegation and does not show the assurance was misleading.
Confirms Altman wrote the 2017 line, replying to Musk's ultimatum. This shows the words were said, not that they were misleading or meant as a permanent promise.
OpenAI's interested account that Musk himself pursued a for-profit structure. This weakens the inference of a concealed departure.
The board review summary links the firing to a loss of trust, not to statements to business partners. It neither confirms nor refutes the candor inference.
The 2026 verdict turned on timing and does not resolve the candor question.

reviews.rationale: The complaint does cite a specific, corroborated Altman statement (e1, e2). But the records do not show it was misleading when made; a later policy change is not enough, and the competing account (e3) cuts against it. No finding links the complaint to the board's candor concerns (e4, e5). The support condition is not met, and neither is the contradiction condition.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: The proposition drops 'by any reasonable metric', which strengthens the claim into a universal over measures. The contract does restore this element, so the observation kind is still correct.

contract.note: The plain reading (substantial abandonment across the founding commitments, judged at the post date) is fair. Since 'any reasonable metric' is strong, continuity on any one measure would count against the claim.

evidence.note: The 2015 baseline. It says nothing about operations in 2024.
2019 structure: commercial LP under nonprofit control with capped returns. It is outside the target period and serves as comparison.
The March 2023 GPT-4 report withholds technical details, showing reduced openness. It predates the snapshot.
Reporting from the post date describes a nonprofit with a capped-profit arm and restricted model details. It does not measure practical mission adherence.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows reduced openness and more commercialisation, alongside continued formal nonprofit control with capped returns. The contract says neither legal status nor commercialisation alone settles how the organisation as a whole operated. Only one item (e4) falls in the target period, and it does not measure practical adherence or how well the nonprofit's oversight actually worked. Neither support nor contradiction is established.
